revision_note: Newly added with 8 verified chunks under public domain (2026-07-23, Batch 10). Source: Paul Carus's 1894 synthesis of Pali canonical/commentarial material, chapters 'Sariputta and Moggallana' and 'Sariputta's Faith', fetched directly from the sacred-texts.com etext.

content.text: Sariputta was a Brahman and one of the chiefs of the followers of Sanjaya, leading a religious life together with his friend Moggallana. The two had made a solemn promise to each other: "He who first attains Nirvana shall tell the other one."
content.source_name: Paul Carus, The Gospel of Buddha (1894), ch. "Sariputta and Moggallana"

content.text: Sariputta, seeing the venerable Assaji begging for alms, modestly keeping his eyes to the ground and dignified in deportment, exclaimed: "Truly this samana has entered the right path; I will ask him in whose name he has retired from the world and what doctrine he professes." Assaji replied: "I am a follower of the Buddha, the Blessed One, but being a novice I can tell you the substance only of the doctrine." Said Sariputta: "Tell me, venerable monk; it is the substance I want."
content.source_name: Paul Carus, The Gospel of Buddha (1894), ch. "Sariputta and Moggallana"

content.text: Assaji recited the stanza: "Nothing we seek to touch or see / Can represent Eternity. / They spoil and die: then let us find / Eternal Truth within the mind." Having heard this stanza, Sariputta obtained the pure and spotless eye of truth and said: "Now I see clearly, whatsoever is subject to origination is also subject to cessation."
content.source_name: Paul Carus, The Gospel of Buddha (1894), ch. "Sariputta and Moggallana"

content.text: Sariputta said: "If this be the doctrine I have reached the state to enter Nirvana which heretofore has remained hidden from me." He went to Moggallana and told him, and both said: "We will go to the Blessed One, that he, the Blessed One, may be our teacher." When the Buddha saw the two friends coming from afar, he said to his disciples: "These two monks are highly auspicious."
content.source_name: Paul Carus, The Gospel of Buddha (1894), ch. "Sariputta and Moggallana"

content.text: When the two friends had taken refuge in the Buddha, the Dharma and the Sangha, the Holy One said to his other disciples: "Sariputta, like the first-born son of a world-ruling monarch, is well able to assist the king as his chief follower to set the wheel of the law rolling."
content.source_name: Paul Carus, The Gospel of Buddha (1894), ch. "Sariputta and Moggallana"

content.text: Seeing that many distinguished young men of Magadha left home to lead a religious life under the Buddha, the people were annoyed and murmured: "Gotama Sakyamuni induces fathers to leave their wives and causes families to become extinct." They reviled the bhikkhus: "The great Sakyamuni has come to Rajagaha subduing the minds of men. Who will be the next to be led astray by him?" The Blessed One told the bhikkhus this murmuring would last only seven days, and instructed them to answer: "It is by preaching the truth that Tathagatas lead men. Who will murmur at the wise? Who will blame the virtuous? Who will condemn self-control, righteousness, and kindness?"
content.source_name: Paul Carus, The Gospel of Buddha (1894), ch. "Sariputta and Moggallana"

content.text: Later, at Nalanda, Sariputta came before the Blessed One and declared: "Lord! such faith have I in the Blessed One, that methinks there never has been, nor will there be, nor is there now any other, who is greater or wiser than the Blessed One." When the Buddha asked whether he therefore knew the hearts of all Buddhas past and future, Sariputta answered: "Not so, O Lord!" each time, then explained: "I only know the lineage of the faith" -- comparing himself to a watchman at a city's one gate who cannot see every crevice in the ramparts, yet knows that all beings of consequence must pass through that single gate. The Buddha replied: "Great is thy faith, O Sariputta, but take heed that it be well grounded."
content.source_name: Paul Carus, The Gospel of Buddha (1894), ch. "Sariputta's Faith"

content.text: This entry compiles verified passages from two chapters of Paul Carus's The Gospel of Buddha (Chicago: Open Court Publishing Co., 1894), a public-domain (pre-1923) synthesis of Pali canonical and commentarial sources hosted on sacred-texts.com: "Sariputta and Moggallana" (btg23.htm), covering his conversion via Assaji's teaching and his ordination alongside Moggallana, and "Sariputta's Faith" (btg90.htm), his dialogue with the Buddha at Nalanda. Both chapters were fetched and quoted verbatim/near-verbatim. Sariputta's traditional epithet "foremost in wisdom" and the canonical account of his death (preceding the Buddha's own parinirvana) are well attested in the wider Pali canon but are not covered by these two specific source chapters and are therefore omitted here rather than asserted without a fetched citation.
content.source_name: Paul Carus, The Gospel of Buddha (1894)
